title: useChartTheme never restyles on a theme toggle, which its own comment promises
foundBy: consumer report (host): an application consuming this package, reported alongside the palette request in CUI-084

evidence.verified:
Three new tests cover the reported failure: a second `useTheme` moves when the first sets a mode, a separate component re-renders when a `ThemeToggle` flips, and a `useChartTheme` consumer gets a fresh theme object when a toggle elsewhere changes the theme. Reverting only `src/lib/useTheme.ts` and rerunning fails all three, so they measure the fix rather than its presence.

`npx vitest run src/lib/useTheme.test.tsx` passes 19 tests. The five suites that touch the theme, which are `useTheme`, `ThemeToggle`, `storageKey`, `chartTheme` and `chartTheme.text`, pass 35 tests between them with no change to any of them.

Measured in the published build rather than the source: `dist/lib/useTheme.js` contains `useSyncExternalStore` and the store map, and `dist/lib/chartTheme.js` still imports the hook. The root bundle grows 834 bytes raw and 319 gzipped, recorded in `preview/src/data/subpath-sizes.json` and inside the existing budget.

`npm run ci` exits 0 at a6766df, with the visual gate comparing 112 of 112 captures at 0 differing pixels and no axe rule matching more nodes.

details:
`useChartTheme` cannot do what it documents. Charts stay in whatever theme was active when they mounted.

`src/lib/useTheme.ts` holds the chosen mode in a plain `useState` with no React context. Its initial value is read once, from the URL parameter or from `localStorage`. Nothing subscribes to later changes.

So each caller gets an independent copy of the state. `src/components/ThemeToggle.tsx` calls it at line 25 and `src/lib/chartTheme.ts` calls it again at line 83. The toggle sets `data-theme` on the root element and writes `localStorage`, but the chart's own copy of `mode` never changes.

`src/lib/chartTheme.ts` re-reads the CSS variables in an effect keyed on `resolved`, at lines 86 to 88. That value is derived from the copy of `mode` that never changes, so the effect never fires again after mount.

The comment above the function, at lines 136 to 139, says it "re-reads the CSS variables whenever the resolved theme flips, so charts restyle on light/dark toggle".

The reporter verified this in the published 0.3.0 build, in `dist/lib/chartTheme.js` and `dist/lib/useTheme.js`, rather than in the source alone.

Either shape fixes it. `useTheme` could hold its state in a context provider, or `useChartTheme` could observe `data-theme` on the root element with a `MutationObserver`.

notes.text:
Two things narrow the blast radius without excusing it. A chart mounted after a toggle reads the stored mode at mount and gets the right theme, so only charts already on screen freeze. And the reporter works around it by putting `var(--token)` directly in the SVG and letting the cascade resolve it, which works.

The cost is that the documented bridge goes unused. A consumer who follows the documentation instead gets charts that silently stop matching the page.

A fourth test was written and is not evidence. It asserts that the store drops its adopted mode when the last caller unmounts, so a later mount reads storage again. It passes against the old code as well, because a per-caller `useState` re-read storage on every mount by construction.

It stays because it guards a risk the fix introduces rather than one it removes. State that lives in a module outlives the components that read it, and a store that kept a mode across mounts would answer a later reader from a session that had ended.

The snapshot is the string `mode|resolved` rather than an object, for two reasons worth keeping. `useSyncExternalStore` compares snapshots by identity, so returning a fresh object on every call loops it. And `mode` on its own does not change when the operating system moves between light and dark under `system`, so a snapshot of the mode alone would hold every caller in the theme the page loaded in, which is a smaller version of the defect this record is about.
